newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Pending peg boosts demand on Bulgaria depo market.
newsitem.headline: Pending peg boosts demand on Bulgaria depo market.

text.p: Demand for lev funds was high on the Bulgarian interbank deposit market on Thursday ahead of a currency board peg as depo rates were unchanged from Wednesday, dealers said.

"Banks are actively seeking levs, probably for foreign currency buying to profit when a currency board is introduced next week. Yields on forex purchases made at today's rates will be higher than yields on government securities," a dealer said.
Traders said that end-month and end-quarter tax and salary payments also boosted demand for funds.

The lev traded at around 991-995 per mark on the local forex market at midday on Thursday, four days before the lev is pegged at a fixed exchange rate of 1,000 per mark from July 1 under a currency board system.
The average yield to maturity on four-week discount T-bills, auctioned daily by the Finance Ministry, fell to 0.40 percent at Wednesday's auction.
Overnight interbank depo rates were flat on Wednesday's 11-12 percent annually. The simple annual interest rates for borrowing for up to seven days were 15-16 percent, also flat.
The average annual interbank deposit rate was 15.10 percent on Wednesday against 14.83 percent on Tuesday, a central bank official said.

The simple monthly main interest rate now is 1.266 percent under the central bank effective annual main interest rate of 16.30 percent that took effect from Monday, central bank figures showed. -- Dessislava Popova, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
